questions: Which floor is it on, what kind of home and what type of apartment is it?
Is it under a roof terrace or above technical spaces?
What is the main orientation and is it open on two sides?
What usable area, ceiling height and layout does it have?
Is there a balcony or a loggia?
What do the accessible walls, ceilings and floors look like?
How do the windows and the interior and entrance doors close?

systems.label: Systems

systems.title: What can be observed in the accessible systems?
questions: What do the exposed wiring and the visible fuse board look like?
What does the exposed plumbing look like?

Is there air conditioning and what type of heating is indicated?

comfort.label: Comfort
comfort.caption: Noise during the visit, traffic and useful places near the home.
comfort.title: How does the home feel and what is nearby?
questions: What ambient noise can be heard during the visit?
Is the home exposed to heavy traffic?
Is there a grocery shop nearby?

Is there a hospital or clinic within 1 km?

risks.label: Risks

risks.title: Which signs need attention or further checks?
questions: Are there visible signs of damp or rising damp?
Are there signs of recent cosmetic cover-up worth clarifying?

Are there unusual smells in the apartment or under the accessible sinks?
Is access difficult or are neighbourhood problems visible?
What additional observations does the inspector note and what could not be checked?

finding.kicker: Example from a Property Fizic report
finding.title: See what a real finding looks like
finding.text: Window, damp or systems: the observation, the impact, the recommendation and the photos.
finding.intro: A fictional example shows how we turn a check into an observation, a possible impact, a recommendation and the related photo.
finding.photoAlt: Illustrative image of an inspector photographing a window frame in an apartment
finding.eyebrow: From the visit to the report
finding.heading: Example of a finding in the report.
finding.reportIntro: Every finding shows the inspection method, the observation, the possible impact and the recommended action.

windows.title: The window does not close evenly.
windows.method: Visual examination and a manual open–close test.
windows.observation: The sash touches the frame in the lower corner and the handle resists when closing. Part of the seal has come loose.
windows.impact: Possibly reduced airtightness and thermal comfort. Air leakage was not measured.
windows.recommendation: Have a joinery specialist check and adjust the closing mechanism, fix the seal and repeat the closing test.
windows.photos: Overview and detail photos of the contact area and the seal, linked to finding F-01.

damp.title: Signs of damp on the wall finish.
damp.method: Visual inspection of the accessible surface; no moisture measurements.
damp.observation: A stain and local paint peeling are visible in the lower corner of the wall. The source of the damp and whether it is active are not confirmed.
damp.impact: The finish is damaged locally. Redoing it may only last a while if the source of the damp remains.
damp.recommendation: Find the source through specialist checks and moisture measurements before redoing the finish.
damp.photos: An overview photo for location and details of the stain and the finish, linked to finding U-01.

systems.title: Connections without visible leaks.
systems.method: Visual examination of the radiator and the accessible connections. The system was not switched on.
systems.observation: No traces of water, deposits or corrosion at the accessible joints at the time of the visit.
systems.impact: The observation describes the visible condition. Pressure tightness and how the heating works remain unconfirmed.
systems.recommendation: An operating test and a check of the connections under working conditions by qualified staff before confirming the condition of the system.
systems.photos: An overview photo and details of the accessible connections, linked to finding I-01.

items.q: What is the difference between Fizic and Online?
items.a: PropertyScore Fizic includes the visit, the inspector's observations, the full online report, the photos, the 360° images and the Polycam plan. For sellers, it also includes preparing the listing on PropertyScore for free. Online includes the area safety score, rent and sale benchmarks and nearby amenities; the condition inside is checked during the visit.

items.q: Do I pay RON 500 or RON 500 + 30?
items.a: RON 500 in total: the inspection, the full online report, the photos, the 360° images, the plan and preparing the listing for sellers are included. The RON 30 is the price of the online report bought on its own.

items.q: What does the area safety score show?
items.a: The PropertyScore score brings together the indicators available for the address's area: context from public data, proximity to services, lighting and surrounding factors, and local reports where available. The report explains the sources, the period and the limits; city-level data is marked as such. The score is a context indicator, not a statistic of incidents at that address.

items.q: What do the average rent and average price in the area mean?
items.a: They are benchmarks from asking rents and prices for comparable apartments, by location and the available characteristics. You see the monthly rent, the asking price per apartment and the price per m² separately, with the source, the period and the area analysed. When the data is not enough for a meaningful average, the report says so. The values in the example on this page are fictional.

items.q: What does the RON 30 online report include?
items.a: Six chapters about the area: education, health, transport, shopping and services, green spaces, safety and quiet. You get the explained safety score, rent and sale benchmarks from comparable listings and a map of useful places. Distances and walking times appear where routing data is available. Every result shows its source and period; insufficient data is flagged explicitly.

items.q: What information do I need for the online analysis?
items.a: The location of the apartment is essential: the address and confirming the point on the map. Rooms, area, floor, lift, parking or heating are optional details. You can continue even if you do not know them.

items.q: Is it useful if I want to rent?
items.a: Yes. You can compare the asking rent with benchmarks for similar apartments and see the safety score, transport, parks and services nearby. The actual condition of the apartment has to be checked separately.

items.q: What can and can't the inspection confirm?
items.a: The report documents what could be observed or checked during the visit and marks the limits. The inspection does not replace a structural survey, a legal check or full testing of the systems.

items.q: What do I get as a buyer?
items.a: With PropertyScore Fizic you get the inspection report, the full online report, the photos, the presentation plan and the 360° tour. The materials are available to you even if the home is not published on PropertyScore. Preparing the listing is an extra benefit for sellers, included in the same package.

items.q: What are the plan and the 360° tour for?
items.a: During the visit we photograph every room with a 360° camera and make the presentation plan with Polycam. A click on a room in the plan takes you through an animated transition to its panorama. Buyer and seller get these materials in the physical package, whether or not the property is published. For sellers, we also include them in the listing we prepare. The example here uses static photos and a schematic plan; the presentation plan is not cadastral.

items.q: Can I publish a listing for free without PropertyScore?
items.a: Yes, publishing your own listing is free. For sale or rent, you can add the photos, the description and the details of the home, and the listing appears in the list and on the property map. The report is optional; without it, the listing is marked “No report”. If you choose PropertyScore Fizic for a sale, we prepare the professional presentation for free in the RON 500 package.

items.q: How do I get the professional listing included in Fizic?
items.a: If you are selling and choose PropertyScore Fizic, we create a professional listing for free from the photos, the plan and the 360° images taken during the visit. The listing brings together the physical report and the full online report, organised around the property. Once you confirm publication, it appears in the listings and on the PropertyScore map. Preparing it is included in the RON 500.
